transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-28 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Lena, Samir; Aisha, Markus, Priya

Summary: Quick intro, then 30m console demo, then deep questions on costs, SLOs, and security, wrap with next steps.

[00:00] Lena Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena, AE on the Redwood Inference team. With me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How are you all?

[00:10] Aisha Khan: Hi Lena, thanks. We're excited; Concordia is evaluating how to attribute inference spend to product routes for Q2 budget planning.

[00:22] Samir Patel: Great. Today we'll show the Console's Usage Lenses and the per-route cost map, how you can map tokens to features and then to cost buckets. We'll also show routing policies between hosted and dedicated.

[00:40] Markus Li: Quick thing up front — our primary constraints are P99 latency under 350ms for clinical flows, data residency in us-west-2, and SOC2-type logs. We also want a predictable monthly commit if dedicated is cheaper.

[00:58] Lena Morales: Perfect, that's helpful. We'll point out the SLA screens and the audit log integration with KMS; also we'll flag where RBAC groups live.

[01:12] Samir Patel: Opening the Console now — apologies if the screen share is a bit laggy. So in the Usage Lenses view you can switch between "by route", "by model", and "by customer token". I'm clicking the route lens — you can see a heatmap of token counts across routes.

[01:35] Aisha Khan: Mm hm, does that include streaming tokens and function calls?

[01:41] Samir Patel: Yes, it collapses streaming deltas into total token consumption; function invocation tokens are included but we tag them separately so you can filter those out if you want. Sometimes the auto-transcription labels function call tokens as "fn-calls" which is not always perfect.

[02:05] Priya Desai: Quick clarification — we have about 12 product routes: triage, note-summarization, med-coding, patient Q&A, and some internal tooling. We want to see which routes are the cost drivers.

[02:18] Samir Patel: Right, back on the Route Cost Map — each route is a bubble sized by total token spend and colored by average latency. You can click into a route, say "note-summarization", and see a breakdown by model variant, sequence length distribution, and quantization profile.

[02:45] Markus Li: Sequence length distribution — can we see percentiles? Like p50/p95 token lengths?

[02:51] Samir Patel: Yep; here's a histogram and a pctl table. This is important because the runtime will choose kernels and batching for the common shapes. For example, if p95 is 1,600 tokens we recommend a different model variant or a different batch config to keep p99 latency under 350ms.

[03:14] Aisha Khan: How do you attribute the cache hits? We use prefix caching for some flows so upstream token counts are lower.

[03:22] Samir Patel: Good question. We show raw request tokens and net tokens after KV cache hits. The Console has a toggle "include cached tokens". By default we show net tokens billed. Note that sometimes the transcription will label KV cache as "K V c ask" in exports — small quirk in the auto transcript.

[03:42] Lena Morales: Also want to call out our Optimize recommendations — rollout suggests batching window, quantization, and whether to move a route to a dedicated pool. Samir will demo that for med-coding.

[03:58] Samir Patel: Jumping to recommendations: med-coding route — high cost per token because p95 sequences are long and it's hitting the high-accuracy model. Optimize suggests: switch to a 7B quantized model for draft pass and run high-accuracy only for finalize step, set batching target to 4, and enable prefix caching for repetitive prompts.

[04:25] Markus Li: If we switch to a quantized variant for part of the flow, how do you handle fallbacks when quality degrades?

[04:33] Samir Patel: We have rollout policies and automatic A/B canaries; you can define a failure threshold (quality regression or latency exceed) and Redwood will fall back to the pinned variant. Console shows an expected cost delta and estimated latency delta for each recommendation.

[04:52] Priya Desai: Where do audit logs go? We need them forwarded to our SIEM and also kept for 12 months for compliance.

[04:59] Lena Morales: We integrate with S3-archival and CloudWatch/Datadog. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and you control retention. For hosted we can push logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules. We'll share the security FAQ.

[05:20] Aisha Khan: Is there a per-route SLA? We have a few high-priority clinical routes where we need a tighter SLO.

[05:27] Samir Patel: You can create per-route SLOs in the Console — the routing policy can prioritize those routes to dedicated capacity or a higher-tier instance class. We also surface estimated tail latencies per model/route from our benchmarks.

[05:45] Lena Morales: I'm going to show the cost explorer now — switch to cost view, here you can group by route, team, or project. You can attribute multi-tenant usage back to feature flags or API keys.

[06:02] Markus Li: We use feature flags in LaunchDarkly — can you join by key?

[06:07] Samir Patel: Yes, we accept arbitrary tags and keys in the request metadata; those appear in the explorer and can be used for slices. We have a demo sheet where we mapped LaunchDarkly flags to route tags.

[06:22] Priya Desai: Is there a recommended commit level for dedicated capacity? We'd like predictable unit economics if we commit monthly.

[06:31] Lena Morales: Dedicated is priced by reserved vGPU pools and you can set burst capacity. We usually run a sizing exercise based on your token shapes; after the benchmark we can propose commit levels. For many customers, a mixed model — hosted for low-frequency routes and dedicated for high-throughput clinical routes — hits the best $/latency tradeoff.

[06:55] Aisha Khan: Let's drill into a specific route — note-summarization. Show us the per-route dashboard, please.

[07:03] Samir Patel: Clicking note-summarization — here's the timeline: tokens per minute, average latency, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens. You can apply a time-range filter to compare pre/post-deploys. There's also a table showing top prompts and their average token lengths.

[07:27] Markus Li: The top prompt table would be useful for cost optimization — can we export that as CSV?

[07:33] Samir Patel: Yes, export CSV or JSON. Note: sometimes the export header has mis-encoded characters in older browsers but we fixed that in the latest patch.

[07:46] Priya Desai: On billing — can charges be routed to different cost centers? Our finance team wants a monthly chargeback by product line.

[07:55] Lena Morales: The billing export includes tags; you can configure cost center tags per API key so finance gets a breakdown. We also provide per-route and per-team billing reports for exports.

[08:10] Aisha Khan: About security docs — can you share SOC2 Type II report and details on encryption at rest/in transit?

[08:18] Lena Morales: Yes, Samir will add standard security pack to the follow-up email including SOC2 artefacts, encryption diagrams, and how KMS is integrated. For Private customers we support HSM-backed keys.

[08:33] Samir Patel: Switching to the Routing Policies screen — you can set a policy that routes clinical.* to DedicatedPool-A (pinned model variant), while routing public.QA to Hosted-LowCost. The policy engine supports weight-based traffic split and latency thresholds.

[08:52] Markus Li: How are fallbacks handled if DedicatedPool-A is saturated during a spike?

[08:58] Samir Patel: If capacity is saturated, the policy can automatically fail over to a compatible hosted variant. You can set hard-fail or soft-fail rules; soft-fail allows response but warns and tags the request. Our Console will highlight incidents where failover occurred and show cost delta for those requests.

[09:20] Priya Desai: We have a concern about PII — some prompts include identifiable info. Does Redwood offer redaction or tokenization before logs are stored?

[09:29] Lena Morales: We offer client-side redaction hooks and server-side redaction before logs persist. With Private deployments you can intercept logs and apply your own transforms. We'll include the redaction options in the security doc.

[09:46] Aisha Khan: Ok, ROI question — can you show an example of what a recommended routing change saved for a similar customer?

[09:54] Samir Patel: Sure, here's an anonymized case study: a health SaaS moved their high-frequency auto-summarization to a quantized 7B draft variant plus a finalize step on a 13B full variant. They reduced monthly inference spend by ~48% while retaining evaluation metrics within 1.8% of baseline. The Console shows the estimated cost delta before you apply changes.

[10:20] Lena Morales: I'm going to show the pilot workflow — we run a 5–7 day benchmark capturing throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token distributions, and end-to-end quality checks on your eval set. We instrument telemetry into your staging environment and produce a sizing recommendation.

[10:45] Markus Li: For the benchmark, what's required from our side? We can provide anonymized traces and an eval set of 500 examples.

[10:53] Samir Patel: That's perfect. We'll need sample traces, API keys for staging, and a short runbook. We'll synthesize traffic shapes and run both hosted and dedicated comparisons.

[11:08] (murmur) Speaker 3: /interrupt — are you able to show a live failover event?

[11:12] Samir Patel: We can simulate one in the sandbox; I can also share a recorded failover incident from a demo tenant later.

[11:22] Priya Desai: One last technical: does the runtime support mixed precision across layers for quantized models? We saw mention of quan-loose in a blog but wanted details.

[11:32] Samir Patel: The runtime supports per-layer quantization profiles; Optimize suggests a profile based on your eval set and latency needs. We'll include a technical note on quantization strategies.

[11:46] Aisha Khan: Ok great. To recap — we'll get the ROI workbook, security pack, and a pilot runbook. We'll send anonymized per-route traces, and we'd like the pilot scheduled week of Feb 9.

[12:02] Lena Morales: Sounds good. I'll follow up with the package and a calendar invite for the kickoff. Anything else?

[12:10] Markus Li: No, that's it from us. Thanks.

[12:14] Lena Morales: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

[12:18] Meeting end

Note: Transcript has occasional mis-hearings and speaker attribution may be approximate; auto-transcript sometimes splits names or misformats acronyms (e.g., VPC -> VCP, KV cache -> K V c ask).
